clue.text: American diffidence where dollars are involved

parts.note: federal describes the US national government, so it can stand for American
reserve is shyness or reticence, a synonym for diffidence

explanation.surface: A remark on Americans being oddly shy when money comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the US central bank is where dollars are issued and controlled.
explanation.definitionFit: The US central banking system controls the supply of dollars, so it is the institution where dollars are involved.

clue.text: Amicable source of warmth that can be lethal

definitions.text: Amicable source of warmth that can be lethal

parts.note: amicable means friendly, well disposed
a fire in the hearth warms a room

explanation.surface: A cosy hearth that turns out to be deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting from one's own side in battle is called this, and it can kill comrades by accident.

clue.text: Stars manage without motoring organisation

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to manage is to do, as in 'we'll do somehow'
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A celebrity coping without roadside breakdown cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: DO goes round RAC. The RAC is a British motoring organisation offering breakdown cover.
explanation.definitionFit: This constellation, the Dragon, is a group of stars in the northern sky.

clue.text: Back pay given new priority

parts.note: swap the order of the words 'back pay' so 'pay' comes first, giving the idiom 'pay back', meaning take revenge

explanation.surface: Arrears of wages being moved up the list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back pay' looks like owed wages; reorder the two words and you get 'pay back', to hit back at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay someone back is to take revenge, which is to strike back in return for a wrong.

clue.text: Ladies one might have formed a connection with

indicators.note: these letters might form something else, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A man musing on women he might have got involved with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' is the anagram signal: LADIES plus I rearranged; 'have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to work in contact with someone, so this past form means made a link with.

clue.text: Rubs out spot embodying greasy spoon repulsion

indicators.note: being pushed back, so the whole assembly is turned round
one word holds the other within its body

parts.note: to spot something is to see it
a caff is British slang for a cheap cafe, a greasy spoon

explanation.surface: Someone scrubbing marks away, put off by a grimy cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE holding CAFF makes SECAFFE; 'repulsion' turns all of it back to front. A caff (greasy spoon) is a cheap British cafe serving fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface something is to erase or wipe it out, a synonym of rubbing out.

clue.text: Zola doesn't end without a message

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so the shortened name goes round the other piece
the name loses its final letter

parts.note: the French novelist Zola's first name was Emile

explanation.surface: The French novelist left unfinished without a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't end' cuts EMILE to EMIL; 'without' (outside) puts EMIL round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail is a message sent over the internet, so the word names such a message.

clue.text: Can active culture protect against disease?

indicators.note: as in a culture grown in a lab, the letters are cultivated into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking whether a live bacterial culture can immunise people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'culture' is the anagram signal for CAN plus ACTIVE; fittingly, vaccines are made from cultures.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaccinate is to inoculate someone so that they become immune to an illness.

clue.text: Paint spray is not appropriate

indicators.note: spraying scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that spray-painting is unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spray' is the anagram signal for PAINT; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or ill-fitting, the same as inappropriate.

clue.text: Give one a ring

parts.note: reads as making a phone call, but means placing an engagement ring on someone's finger

explanation.surface: Telephone somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: The phone-call reading is the misdirection; the ring is an engagement ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To affiance is to betroth, and an engagement is marked by giving a ring.

clue.text: Flyer turns to Meryl Streep out east

indicators.note: the letters turn about into a new order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An airline passenger turning towards the actress, heading out east.
explanation.walkthrough: TO plus MERYL STREEP has one E too many: 'out east' removes an E, and 'turns' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: This small seabird, said to herald storms, is a flyer over the ocean.

clue.text: Idiots — old ones possibly

indicators.note: suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Saying fools may well be elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' is the anagram signal for OLD ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is informal for a silly person, so the plural means fools.

clue.text: One takes a bow, still shaky after church

indicators.note: the anagram comes after the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

indicators.note: unsteady letters wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer, still trembling, bows at the end of a church concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaky' rearranges STILL; 'after church' puts it behind CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A string player draws a bow across the instrument, a pun on bowing to applause.

clue.text: Party unknown to a foreign country

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A political party strange to some country abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This North African nation is a country foreign to British readers.

clue.text: Book of Life

parts.note: sounds like a sacred register, but means a book telling the story of someone's life

explanation.surface: The heavenly register of the saved.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L suggests the Book of Life in Revelation; it is just a life story.
explanation.definitionFit: A written account of a person's life is a book about that life.

clue.text: Resort to the nether regions and corruption

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, the realm of the dead
to resort to a place is to repair there, go there

explanation.surface: Going to hell and moral decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort to' means go, as 'repair to' does; Dis is the classical underworld. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Corruption in the sense of decay matches a state of neglect and ruin.

clue.text: Embracing clairvoyance, employing nothing intermediate

indicators.note: placed in between the other two pieces

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception
employing means using
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Taking up psychic powers without using anything in between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermediate' puts O between ESP and USING.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousing a cause means adopting or embracing it.

clue.text: French — base breed, rough but cultivated

parts.note: base in the sense of mean or vulgar is low

indicators.note: roughed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Frenchman of humble, coarse stock who is nonetheless refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges BREED to ERBED; 'but' is a link. The definition is loose: a flowerbed is a cultivated patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot dug and planted in a garden is ground that is cultivated, so the definition is descriptive.

clue.text: City (part urban) liable to spread?

indicators.note: spreading the letters about rearranges them
only a portion of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a city, partly built up, tends to sprawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' takes URB from URBAN; 'liable to spread' rearranges CITY plus URB. The acid is found in butter, which spreads.
explanation.definitionFit: This acid gives rancid butter its smell, and butter is a spread.

clue.text: Sound measure of tenth Babylonian deity?

parts.note: deci- is the prefix for a tenth
Bel was a Babylonian god

explanation.surface: Asking how loud a minor Babylonian god might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The unit really is a tenth of a bel; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This unit measures the intensity of sound, so it is a measure of loudness.

clue.text: Ruth contains first example of devotion

indicators.note: Ruth's word contains the next piece, holding that letter within itself

parts.note: ruth is an archaic word for pity

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The Book of Ruth holds a model of faithfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth looks like the name; lower-case ruth means pity, the root of ruthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devotion, a reverence for God.

clue.text: Arbiter of cooked delicacy

indicators.note: cooking mixes things up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge of fine food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges ARBITER; 'of' is a link. Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit, melted cheese on toast, is a savoury dish, loosely a delicacy.

clue.text: Rising friction over small vehicle's personal cover

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits above the second
in a down entry the word goes upward, read backwards

parts.note: a rub is a source of friction
the Ka was a small Ford car

explanation.surface: Chafing over a little car's cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns RUB upward to BUR; 'over' puts it above KA, a small Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: This full-body garment worn by some Muslim women covers the wearer completely.

clue.text: Nazi thugs in vulgar military expedition

indicators.note: one piece set within the other

parts.note: vulgar means crude
the SA, the Sturmabteilung, were the Nazi brownshirt stormtroopers

explanation.surface: Fascist brutes taking part in a coarse military campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The SA were the Nazi brownshirts.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval Christian wars to win the Holy Land were military expeditions.

clue.text: Grotesque figure derived from the manticore

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A monster image based on the mythical man-eating beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'manticore'.
explanation.definitionFit: Antic as a noun is an old word for a grotesque or a clown.

clue.text: It was the making of the first lady

definitions.text: It was the making of the first lady

parts.words: It was the making of the first lady
parts.note: in Genesis Eve was made from one of Adam's ribs, left over and so not needed

explanation.surface: Something that made the president's wife what she is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' suggests a president's wife; it is Eve, made from Adam's rib.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's rib, which he could spare, was used to create Eve, the first woman.

clue.text: Plant when season's not begun

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: winter is a season

explanation.surface: Sowing a seed before the season has started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like gardening; here it means bury. 'not begun' drops W from WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant a body in the ground is to bury it, which is to inter.

clue.text: Once gay, perhaps with reason to do with women

indicators.note: suggests the letters may be ordered otherwise

parts.note: logical means having reason

explanation.surface: Someone who was once gay, perhaps for a good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ONCE GAY into GYNAEC.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of medicine deals with women's reproductive health.
